item: A restore places a carried signing key wrapped under this install's passphrase, and never over a key that is there (R448)
key_paths: src/backup/merge.py; src/backup/artifact.py; src/backup/stream_backup.py; src/backup/import_reports.py; tests/test_restore_key_rewrap.py; tests/test_shared_file_writes.py
summary: merge_side_files placed keys/ as carried (wrapped under the source install's passphrase, which blocked every export here) with exists() then os.replace (a key an export made in between was overwritten). _restore_key_members opens each carried Ed25519/ML-DSA key with this install's held passphrase, then the source corpus's and the backup's (StagedArtifact.key_passphrases, repr=False, set by read_artifact/read_volume_backup/read_stream_backup), seals it the way this install writes its own, reads it back before writing, and places it with keyfile.create_new (no clobber); a key none of them opens is not written, is named in report keys.not_placed and in the import report's 'Signing keys not restored' section; a signer's Ed25519 + ML-DSA pair is placed whole or not at all, and not at all when this install has either half. On an install that holds no passphrase a carried encrypted key is placed exactly as carried, never in the clear (R613), and the import report's 'Signing keys still encrypted' section says to set OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE and restart; each Ed25519 key placed is named with its public key ('Signing identity taken from the backup'); a pair the disk refuses halfway leaves neither half (only the files this call made, matched by device and inode); manifest names are escaped in the report.
